volume: 第三卷術業部 Volume 3: Arts and Professions Department

stories.text: 醫人買得醫官札付者，冠帶而坐於店中。過者駭曰：「此何店，而有官在內？」傍人答曰：「此醫官之店。」
stories.translation: A medical person named Maidé, who had received a certificate from the medical office, wore a hat and sat in the shop. Passersby were startled and said, "What kind of shop is this, that it has an official inside?" A bystander answered, "This is the shop of a medical official."

stories.title_en: The King of Hell seeks a famous physician.
stories.text: 冥王遣鬼卒訪陽間名醫，命之曰：「門前無冤鬼者即是。」鬼卒領旨，來到陽世，每過醫門，冤鬼畢集。最後至一家，見門首獨鬼彷徨，曰：「此可以當名醫矣。」問之，乃昨日新豎藥牌者。
stories.translation: The King of Hell sent ghostly attendants to seek out the most renowned physicians in the mortal world, instructing them, "He who has no vengeful ghosts before his door is the one." The ghostly attendants accepted their orders and came to the mortal world. Every time they passed by a physician's door, vengeful ghosts gathered in full. Finally, they arrived at one house and saw only a single ghost lingering uncertainly by the door. They said, "This man can be considered a renowned physician." When asked, it turned out to be someone who had just yesterday newly set up a medicine signboard.

stories.text: 一醫生醫死人，主家憤甚，呼群僕毒打。醫跪求至再，主曰：「私打可免，官法難饒。」即命送官懲治。醫畏罪，哀告曰：「願僱人抬往殯殮。」主人許之。醫苦家貧，無力僱募，家有二子，夫妻四人共來抬柩。至中途，醫生嘆曰：「為人切莫學行醫。」妻咎夫曰：「為你行醫害老妻。」幼子云：「頭重腳輕抬不起。」長子曰：「爹爹，以後醫人揀瘦的。」
stories.translation: A physician killed a patient, and the family was extremely angry, calling upon their servants to beat him severely. The doctor repeatedly begged for mercy on his knees, but the family said, "Private punishment may be forgiven, but official justice cannot spare you." They immediately ordered him to be sent to the authorities for punishment. Fearing punishment, the doctor mournfully pleaded, "I wish to hire people to carry him away for burial." The family agreed. The doctor was poor and unable to afford hiring people, so he sent his two sons along with himself and his wife—four people in total—to carry the coffin. Halfway through the journey, the doctor sighed and said, "When one wishes to be a person, never learn to become a physician." His wife scolded him, saying, "Because of your medical practice, it has harmed an old wife like me." The younger son said, "It's too heavy on top and light at the bottom; we can't lift it up." The older son said, "Father, in the future, when you treat people, choose thin ones."

stories.text: 有送醫士出門，犬適攔門而吠，主人喝之即止。醫贊其能解人意，主曰：「雖則畜生，倒也還會依（醫）人。」
stories.translation: Someone sent a medical practitioner out the door, and just then a dog happened to block the entrance and barked. The owner shouted at it, and it stopped. The physician praised the dog's ability to understand human intent. The owner said, "Although it is an animal, it can actually follow (a doctor)."

stories.text: 一人向醫家買春藥吃了。行至半路，藥性發作，此物翹然直豎。乃以手捧住贊曰：「好郎中，好郎中，好郎中！」
stories.translation: A man bought aphrodisiacs from a physician's shop and took them. While walking halfway, the medicine's effects kicked in, causing this organ to rise upright. He then held it up with his hands and praised, "A good physician! A good physician! A good physician!"

stories.text: 有害赤眼者，百方治之不效。或教以用尿除頭去尾，抹之即好，如言用後果愈。一日小便，手握陽具而言曰：「虧你醫好我眼，欲折頂巾你戴，你頭忽大忽小，做件衣你穿，你身時長時短。」人問為何自言自語，答曰：「我在此打點謝郎中。」
stories.translation: A person suffering from red eyes tried many remedies without success. Someone advised using urine, removing the head and tail, applying it would cure; following this advice indeed resulted in recovery. One day, while urinating, he held his penis and said, "You helped cure my eyes; I wanted to make a cap for you to wear. Your head is sometimes big and sometimes small. I want to sew a robe for you to wear, but your body is at times long and at times short." People asked why he was talking to himself. He replied, "I am here preparing a thank-you for Physician Xie."

stories.text: 一人有一妻二妾，死後，妻妾繞屍而哭。妻撫其首，曰：「我的郎頭呀！」次捏其足，曰：「我的郎腳呀！」又次者無可哭附，只得握其陽物曰：「我的郎中呀！」
stories.translation: A man had one wife and two concubines. After his death, the wife and concubines wept around his corpse. The wife caressed his head and said, "My dear husband's head!" Then she grasped his foot and said, "My dear husband's feet!" The next one had nothing else to weep over or cling to, so she could only grasp his penis and say, "My dear physician!"

stories.text: 一士人往花園遊玩，見籬邊薔薇盛開，嬌媚可人。近前攀折，被薔薇刺破手指，出血不止。偶遇一牧童，言曰：「血不止，可將熱尿淋之即好。」士依其言，血果即止。遂作口號以贊之曰：「今朝散步入園中，窺見薔薇滿樹紅。雙手摘時遭一刺，血流不止手鮮紅。牧童傳把熱尿淋，果然滅跡就無蹤。莫道人間無妙藥，屪子也會做郎中。」
stories.translation: A scholar went to the garden for recreation and saw that roses were in full bloom by the fence, charming and delightful. As he stepped closer to pluck one, a thorn pricked his finger, causing it to bleed continuously. He happened to meet a herdsboy who said, "If the blood won't stop flowing, you can pour hot urine over it and it will be fine." The scholar followed his advice, and indeed the bleeding stopped. He then composed a verse to praise him: "Today I strolled into the garden, where I saw red roses blooming on every tree. While plucking them with both hands, I was pricked by a thorn; blood flowed nonstop and my hand turned bright red." The herdsboy told me to pour hot urine over it, and indeed the wound vanished without a trace. "Do not say there are no miraculous remedies in this world; even a donkey's penis can act as a physician."

stories.text: 一方士專賣迷婦人藥，婦著在身，自來與人私合。一日，有輕浪子弟來買藥，適方士他出，其妻取藥付之。子弟就以藥彈其身上。隨婦至房，婦只得與伊交合。方士歸，妻以其事告之。方士怒云：「誰教你就他？」妻曰：「我若不從，顯得你的藥便不靈了。」
stories.translation: A certain Daoist specialist sold drugs that bewitched women. When a woman wore the drug on her body, she would secretly engage in relationships with others. One day, a fickle young man came to buy the drug, but just then the Daoist was away. His wife took the medicine and gave it to him. The young man immediately applied the medicine onto his own body. He followed a woman to her room, and she had no choice but to have relations with him. When the Daoist returned, his wife told him about what had happened. The Daoist angrily said, "Who taught you to obey him?" His wife replied, "If I had not complied, it would have made your medicine seem ineffective."

stories.text: 一人賣跳蚤藥，招牌上寫出「賣上好蚤藥」。問：「何以用法？」答曰：「捉住跳蚤，以藥塗其嘴，即死矣。」
stories.translation: A man sold flea medicine, and his signboard read "Selling the finest flea medicine." Someone asked, "How is it used?" He replied, "Catch a flea and apply the medicine to its mouth; it will die immediately."

stories.text: 人家請醫看乳癖，醫將好奶玩弄不已。主駭問何意，答曰：「我在此仔細斟酌，必要醫得與他一樣纔好。」
stories.translation: A family invited a physician to examine a breast tumor, and the doctor kept playing with the healthy breast without stopping. The host was startled and asked what he meant, to which the doctor replied, "I am carefully considering here; I must treat it so that it becomes exactly like the other one."

stories.text: 一人患病，醫家看脈云：「吃了藥，腹中定響，當走大便，不然，定撒些屁。」少頃，坐中忽聞屁聲，醫曰：「如何？」客應云：「是小弟撒的。」醫曰：「也好。」
stories.translation: A man fell ill, and the physician examined his pulse and said, "After taking this medicine, your abdomen will surely rumble. You should have a bowel movement; otherwise, you are bound to pass some gas." A short while later, someone suddenly heard a fart in the room. The physician asked, "How is it?" The guest replied, "It was my younger brother who passed gas." The physician said, "That's also fine."

stories.text: 一按臺患病，接醫診視，醫驚持畏縮，錯看了手背。按院大怒，責而逐之。醫曰：「你打便打得好，只是你脈息俱無了。」
stories.translation: An official of the Inspection Department fell ill and summoned a physician for diagnosis. The doctor was startled, held back in fear, and mistakenly examined his hand's back instead. The Inspectorate Office became very angry and scolded the doctor before expelling him. The physician said, "If you are going to beat me, do it well, but at least your pulse is now gone."

stories.text: 樵夫擔柴，誤觸醫士。醫怒，欲揮拳。樵夫曰：「寧受腳踢，勿動尊手。」傍人誤之，樵者曰：「腳踢未必就死，經了他手，定然難活。」
stories.translation: A woodcutter, carrying firewood, accidentally bumped into a physician. The physician became angry and was about to strike with his fist. The woodcutter said, "Rather be kicked by your feet than have you use your noble hands." A bystander misunderstood, so the woodcutter said, "Being kicked by his feet might not kill me for sure, but if he touches me with his hands, I will certainly be doomed."

stories.text: 一人往觀武場，飛箭誤中其身，迎外科治之。醫曰：「易事耳。」遂用小鋸截其外竿，即索謝辭去。問：「內截如何？」答曰：「此是內科的事。」
stories.translation: A man went to watch a martial arts demonstration, when an arrow accidentally struck him. He was taken to see a surgeon for treatment. The physician said, "It's an easy matter." He then used a small saw to cut off the outer shaft and immediately asked for payment before leaving. Someone asked, "What about the part inside?" He replied, "That is an internal medicine matter."

stories.text: 或見醫者，問以生意何如，答曰：「不要說起，都被算命先生誤了，囑我有病人家不要去走。」
stories.translation: Someone met a physician and asked how his business was. The doctor replied, "Don't even mention it; it has all been ruined by the fortune-teller, who told me not to visit sick people's homes."

stories.text: 有醫死人兒，許以袖歸殯殮，其家恐見欺，命僕隨之。至一橋上，忽取兒屍擲之河內。僕怒曰：「如何拋了我家小舍？」醫曰：「非也。」因舉左袖曰：「你家的在這裏。」
stories.translation: A physician had killed a child and promised to return the body wrapped in his sleeve. The family, fearing deception, ordered their servant to follow him. When they reached a bridge, he suddenly took the child's corpse and threw it into the river. The servant angrily said, "How could you throw away my master's little son?" The physician replied, "No." He then raised his left sleeve and said, "Your son is right here."

stories.text: 一尼欲心甚熾，以蘿蔔代陽，大肆抽送，暢所欲為。不料用力太猛，折其半截在內。挖之不出，漸至腫脹。延醫看視，醫將兩手陰傍按捺，良久突出，剛打在醫人臉上。醫者嘆曰：「我也醫千醫萬，從未見屄會打彈。」
stories.translation: A nun had an intense desire and used a radish to substitute for a penis, vigorously thrusting back and forth, indulging in whatever she desired. Unluckily, she applied too much force and broke half of it inside. She could not remove it, and gradually her body swelled up. They invited a physician to examine the situation. The doctor pressed with both hands on either side for a long time, and finally it popped out, striking the doctor's face directly. The physician sighed and said, "I have treated thousands upon thousands of patients, but I've never seen a vulva that could shoot bullets."

stories.text: 一醫遷居，謂四鄰曰：「向來打攪，無物可做別敬，每位奉藥一帖。」鄰舍辭以無病，醫曰：「但吃了我的藥，自然會生起病來。」
stories.translation: A physician moved house and told his four neighbors, "In the past I have troubled you; there is nothing suitable to offer as a farewell gift. Please accept one prescription of medicine each." The neighbors declined, saying they were not ill. The physician replied, "But after taking my medicine, you will naturally fall ill."

stories.text: 一醫止宿病家，夜半屎急不便，乃出於一箱格中，閉之。晨起，主人請用藥，偶欲抽視此格，醫堅執不許。主人問：「是何藥？」答曰：「我自吃的補藥在內。」
stories.translation: A physician stayed at a patient's home. In the middle of the night, he urgently needed to relieve himself but found it inconvenient and so went into one compartment of a chest, closing it behind him. In the morning, after getting up, the host invited the physician to take medicine. By chance, he wanted to open this compartment for a look, but the physician firmly refused permission. The host asked, "What kind of medicine is it?" He replied, "It contains the tonic I take myself."

stories.text: 一鄉人與城裡人同行，見一妓女，鄉人問：「是誰家宅眷？」城裏人曰：「此藥戶也。」鄉人曰：「原來就是開藥店的家婆。」
stories.translation: A villager and a city dweller traveled together. Seeing a courtesan, the villager asked, "Whose family member is she?" The city dweller said, "This is from a medicine household." The villager said, "So she must be the wife of the pharmacy owner."

stories.text: 有生平未近女色者，不知隂物是何樣範。向人問之，人曰：「就像一隻眼睛豎起便是。」此人牢記在心。一日，嫖興忽發，不知妓館何在，遂向街頭閒撞。見一眼科招牌，上画眼樣數隻，偶然橫放，以為此必妓家也。進內道其來意，醫士大怒，叱而逐之。其人曰：「旣不是妓館，為何擺這許多屄樣在外面。」
stories.translation: There was a man who had never been close to women in his life and did not know what the female genitalia looked like. He asked someone about it, and a person said, "It looks just like an eye standing upright." This man remembered the description carefully. One day, he suddenly felt a strong urge to visit a prostitute but did not know where the brothel was located, so he wandered aimlessly on the street. He saw a signboard for an ophthalmologist with several eye diagrams displayed, one of which was placed horizontally. He mistakenly thought this must be a brothel. When he entered and explained his intention, the physician became very angry and scolded him before driving him out. The man said, "If this is not a brothel, then why are so many vulva-shaped diagrams displayed outside?"

stories.text: 有販賣藥材者，離家數載，其妻已生下四子。一日夫歸，問眾子何來，妻曰：「為你出外多年，我朝暮思君，結想成胎，故命名俱暗藏深意：長是你乍離家室，宿舟沙畔，故名宿砂；次是你遠鄉作客，我在家志念，故名遠志；三是料你置貨完備，合當歸家，故喚當歸；四是連年盼你不到，今該返回故鄉，故喚茴香。」夫聞之，大笑曰：「依你這等說來，我再在外幾年，家裡竟開得一片山藥鋪了。」
stories.translation: There was a merchant who sold medicinal herbs and had been away from home for several years; his wife had already given birth to four sons. One day, the husband returned home and asked where all his sons had come from. The wife said, "Since you have been away for many years, I thought of you morning and night until my thoughts took form as pregnancies; thus, I gave them names with deep meanings: the eldest was born when you first left home, staying on a boat by the sandbank, so his name is Susha (宿砂); the second son was born while you were far from your hometown as a guest, and I remained at home thinking of you, hence his name Yuanzhi (遠志); the third child came about when I thought that you must have finished preparing goods for sale and should return home, so he is called Danggui (當歸); the fourth son was born after many years of waiting for your return without success; now it's time to go back to our hometown, hence his name Huixiang (茴香)." Hearing this, the husband laughed and said, "According to your logic, if I stay away for a few more years, there will be an entire herbal medicine shop at home."

stories.text: 一貧士患腹瀉，請醫調治，謂醫曰：「家貧不能饋藥金，醫好之日，奉請一醉。」醫從之。服藥而愈，恐醫索謝，詐言腹瀉未止。一日，醫者伺其大便，隨往驗之。見撒出者俱是乾糞，因怒指而示之曰：「撤了這樣好糞，如何還不請我？」
stories.translation: A poor scholar suffered from diarrhea and invited a physician for treatment. He told the doctor, "My family is poor and cannot offer money or medicine; on the day you cure me, I will invite you to get drunk." The physician agreed. After taking the medicine and recovering, he was afraid that the doctor would ask for thanks, so he pretended that his diarrhea had not stopped. One day, the physician waited for him to defecate and followed along to examine it. Seeing that what was excreted were all dry feces, the physician angrily pointed at them and said to him, "If you can pass such good feces, how come you still haven't invited me?"

stories.text: 一醫藥死人兒，主家詬之曰：「汝好好殯殮我兒罷了，否則訟之於官。」醫許以帶歸處置，因匿兒於藥箱中。中途又遇一家邀去，啟箱用藥，誤露兒屍。主家驚問，對曰：「這是別人醫殺了，我帶去包活的。」
stories.translation: A physician killed a child with medicine. The family scolded him, saying, "You had better properly bury my son; otherwise, I will report you to the authorities." The physician promised to take the child home for disposal and secretly placed the child in a medicine chest. On the way, he encountered another family who invited him over; when opening the box to take out medicine, he accidentally revealed the child's corpse. The family was shocked and asked about it; he replied, "This is a child killed by another physician; I am taking him to revive him."

stories.text: 有小兒患身熱，請醫服藥而死，父請醫家咎之。醫不信，自往驗視，撫兒屍謂其父曰：「你太欺心，不過要我與他退熱，今身上幸已冰涼的了，倒反來責備我。」
stories.translation: A child fell ill with a high fever and died after taking medicine prescribed by a physician. The father blamed the doctor for it. The physician did not believe it and went to examine the child's body himself, patting the corpse while saying to the father, "You are too untrustworthy. You only wanted me to reduce his fever; now that his body is happily cool, you dare to blame me."

stories.text: 一醫久無生理，忽有求藥者至，開箱取藥，中多蛀蟲。人問：「此是何物？」曰：「疆蠶。」又問：「疆蠶如何是活的？」答曰：「吃了我的藥，怕他不活？」
stories.translation: A physician had long been without income when suddenly a person came seeking medicine. He opened his chest to retrieve it, only to find many insects had infested the drugs. The person asked, "What are these creatures?" He replied, "Desert silkworms." The person asked again, "How do you know these desert silkworms are alive?" He replied, "After eating my medicine, how could they not be alive?"

stories.text: 有醫壞人者，罰牽麥十擔。牽畢，放歸。次日，有叩門者曰：「請先生看脈。」醫應曰：「曉得了。你先去淘淨在那裡，我就來牽也。」
stories.translation: A physician who had harmed someone was punished to carry ten dan of wheat. After completing the task, he was released and allowed to return home. The next day, someone knocked on his door and said, "Please, Master, examine my pulse." The physician replied, "I understand." "Just go and clean it there first; I will come to pull it right away."

stories.text: 醫生、妓女、偷兒三人，死見冥王，王問生前技術。醫士曰：「小人行醫，人有疾病，能起死回生。」王怒曰：「我每常差鬼卒勾提罪人，你反與我把持抗衡，可發往油鍋受罪。」次問妓女，妓曰：「接客。人沒妻室者，與他解渴應急。」王曰：「方便孤身，延壽一紀。」再問偷兒，答曰：「做賊。人家晒浪衣服，散放銀錢，我去替他收拾些。」王曰：「與人分勞代力，也加壽十年，發轉陽世。」醫士急忙哀告曰：「大王若如此判斷，只求放我還陽。家中尚有一子一女，子叫他去做賊，女就呌他接客便了。」
stories.translation: A physician, a courtesan, and a thief died and appeared before the King of Hell. The king asked about their skills in life. The physician said, "I was a medical practitioner; when people were ill, I could bring the dead back to life." The King of Hell angrily said, "I often send spirits to summon criminals for punishment, yet you dared to oppose and resist me. You should be cast into the oil pot to suffer punishment." Next, he asked the courtesan; she said, "Receiving guests." "For those without a wife or spouse, I provide relief and satisfy their needs in an emergency." The King of Hell said, "Convenient for the lonely; you may live twelve more years." Then he asked the thief, who replied, "I was a thief." "When people hang their clothes to dry and leave silver coins scattered, I go to help them tidy things up for them." The King of Hell said, "Assisting others by sharing their labor and effort is also virtuous; I shall grant you an additional ten years of life. Return to the mortal world." The physician hurriedly pleaded, "Great King, if you judge in this way, I only beg for your mercy to let me return to the mortal world. At home, there is still one son and one daughter; I will have my son become a thief and my daughter become a courtesan."

stories.text: 大方脉抓住小兒科痛打，傍人勸曰：「你兩個同道中，何苦如此。」大方脈曰：「列位有所不知，這廝可惡得緊。我醫的大人俱變成孩子與他醫，誰想他醫的孩子，一個也不放大來與我毉。」
stories.translation: A senior physician grabbed a pediatrician and began to beat him. A bystander tried to persuade them, saying, "You are both in the same profession; why be so cruel?" The senior physician said, "Everyone here doesn't know this, but this fellow is extremely despicable." "I treat adults and they all turn into children for him to treat. Yet, he treats the children and not a single one grows up to become an adult for me to treat."

stories.text: 富家延二醫，一大方，一幼科。客至，問：「二位何人？」主人曰：「皆名醫。」又問：「那一科？」主人曰：「這是大方，這個便是小兒。」
stories.translation: A wealthy family invited two physicians, one a senior doctor and the other a pediatrician. When guests arrived, they asked, "Who are these two gentlemen?" The host said, "They are both famous physicians." They asked again, "Which specialty?" The host said, "This one is the senior physician, and this other one is a pediatrician."

stories.text: 小兒科之妻，乃大方脈之女，每每互相譏誚。一夜行房，婦執陽物問夫曰：「此是何物？」夫曰：「大方脈。」夫亦指牝戶問，婦曰：「這是小兒窠。」
stories.translation: The wife of the pediatrician was the daughter of the senior physician, and they often mocked each other. One night during intimacy, the woman took her husband's penis in hand and asked him, "What is this?" Her husband replied, "Senior physician." The husband then pointed to her vulva and asked. The woman said, "This is the pediatric department."

stories.text: 有人畜一金絲小犬，愛同珍寶，恐其天寒凍壞，內外各用小棉褥鋪成一窠，使其好睡。不意此犬一日竟臥于兒籃內，主人見之，大笑曰：「這畜生好作怪，既不走內窠，又不往外窠，倒鑽進小兒窠（科）裡去了。」
stories.translation: A man kept a golden-haired puppy and cherished it as a precious treasure. Afraid that the cold weather might freeze the dog, he lined both inside and outside with small cotton mats to make a nest for it so the dog could sleep comfortably. Unexpectedly, one day the dog ended up lying inside a baby's cradle. The owner saw this and laughed heartily, saying, "This beast is quite mischievous; it neither went into the inner nest nor the outer nest but instead crawled right into the baby's nest (department)."

stories.text: 一醫看病，許以無事。病家費去多金，竟不起，因恨甚，遣僕往罵。少頃歸，問：「曾罵否？」曰：「不曾。」問：「何以不罵？」僕答曰：「要罵要打的人，多得緊在那裡，叫我如何挨擠得上？」
stories.translation: A physician diagnosed an illness and assured the patient that there was nothing to worry about. The patient's family spent a great deal of money, but the condition did not improve; they became very angry and sent a servant to scold him. After some time, he returned home. The family asked, "Did you scold him?" The servant replied, "No." They asked, "Why didn't you scold him?" The servant replied, "There are so many people who want to scold and beat him there that I couldn't even get close."

stories.text: 一醫醫死人兒，主家欲舉訟，願以己子賠之。一日，醫死人僕，家止一僕，又以賠之。夜間又有叩門者云：「娘娘產裡病，煩看。」醫私謂其妻曰：「淘氣！那家想必又看中意你了。」
stories.translation: A physician killed a child, and the family wanted to file a lawsuit. They were willing to offer their own son as compensation. One day, the physician killed the family's servant; there was only one servant in the household, so they offered another to compensate. At night, a knock came at the door with someone saying, "The lady of the house is ill after childbirth; please come and examine her." The physician privately told his wife, "Troublesome!" "That family must have taken a liking to you again."

stories.text: 有終日吃藥而不謝醫者，醫甚憾之。一日，此人問醫曰：「貓生病，吃甚藥？」曰：「吃烏藥。」「然則狗生病，吃何藥？」曰：「吃白藥。」
stories.translation: There was someone who took medicine all day without thanking the physician, which greatly upset the doctor. One day, this person asked the physician, "My cat is sick; what medicine should it take?" łoż The doctor said, "Give it Wu Yao." "Then if a dog is sick, what medicine should be given?" He said, "Give it white medicine."

stories.text: 一醫生醫壞人，為彼家所縛，夜半逃脫，赴水遁歸。見其子方讀《脈訣》，遽謂曰：「我兒讀書尚緩，還是學遊水要緊。」
stories.translation: A physician who had botched a treatment was bound by the family and escaped at midnight, fleeing back home by swimming. Seeing his son reading the "Pulse Essentials," he hastily said, "My son, studying is not urgent; learning to swim is more important."

stories.text: 一風水新婚初夜，手摸著新人鼻梁曰：「此是發龍之所。」又摸其兩乳曰：「喜得龍虎俱全。」再摸至肚上曰：「好一塊平沙。」摸至腰下曰：「好個金井護穴。」及上妻身，問：「汝來何事？」地師曰：「陰地皆由做成，我把羅星來塞水口。」其父隔壁聽見，放聲大笑曰：「既有這等好穴，何不將我老骨頭埋在裡面，蔭些好子孫出來。」
stories.translation: On the first night of his marriage, a geomancer ran his hand along his new bride's nose and said, "This is where the dragon originates." He then touched her two breasts and said, "I am delighted to find both the Dragon and Tiger are complete." Then he touched her abdomen and said, "What a fine stretch of flat sand." Touching down to her waist, he said, "A fine golden well protecting the site." When his wife came in, she asked, "What are you doing here?" The geomancer said, "All the yin sites are made by me; I am using the Luo star to block the water mouth." His father, hearing this from the next room, burst out laughing and said, "If there is such a good site, why not bury my old bones in it to produce some fine descendants."

stories.text: 一風水父子同室。其子與媳欲合，乃從頭摸起曰：「密密層層一座山。」至乳則曰：「兩峰高聳實非凡。」至肚則曰：「中間好塊平陽地。」至陰戶則曰：「正穴原來在此間。」父聽見，乃高叫曰：「我兒有如此好地，千萬留來把我先埋葬在裡面。」
stories.translation: A feng shui master and his son were in the same room. The son, desiring to be intimate with his wife, began touching her from head to toe and said, "A dense and layered mountain." When he reached her breasts, he said, "Two peaks towering high are truly extraordinary." Reaching her abdomen, he remarked, "A fine stretch of flat yang land in the middle." When he reached her genital area, he said, "The true site is right here." Hearing this, the father shouted loudly, "My son has found such a good site; be sure to keep it and bury me there first."

stories.text: 昔一人患膀胱偏墜之症，請醫調治。醫曰：「外腎左邊屬陽，右邊屬陰，今偏於一邊，卻是陰陽不和之故耳。」其人問曰：「既是左屬陽，右屬陰，不知中間危坐者喚作何名？」醫笑曰：「此是看陰陽的先生。」
stories.translation: Long ago, a man suffered from a condition where his bladder was unevenly swollen and he invited a physician to treat him. The doctor said, "The left side of the external kidney belongs to Yang, and the right side belongs to Yin. Now it is swollen on one side; this must be due to an imbalance between Yin and Yang." The man asked, "If the left side belongs to Yang and the right to Yin, I wonder what name is given to the one sitting in the middle?" The doctor laughed and said, "This is the master who observes Yin and Yang."

stories.text: 從來人墮水淹死，飄浮水面，覆者是男，仰者是女。一日，有屍從河內側身汆來者。人見之，皆道：「奇怪！若是女，一定仰，而男則覆轉。今此人側起，男女未知孰是。」傍一人曰：「此必是個陰陽生耳。」
stories.translation: It is said that when people drown and float on the water, those who float face down are men, and those who float on their backs are women. One day, a corpse floated sideways from the river. People saw it and all said, "Strange!" "If it were a woman, she would float on her back; if a man, he would be face down." "Now this person is floating sideways, and we cannot tell whether it's male or female." A man nearby said, "This must be a yinyang master."

stories.text: 無賴子怒一富翁，思所以傾其家而不得。聞有茅山道士法力最高，往訴懇之。道士曰：「我使天兵陰誅此翁。」答：「其子孫仍富，吾不甘也。」曰：「然則，吾縱天火焚其室廬。」答曰：「其田土猶存，吾不甘也。」道士曰：「汝仇深至此乎！吾有一至寶，賜汝持去，朝夕供奉拜求，彼家自然立耗矣。」其人喜甚，請而觀之。封緘甚密，啟視，則紙做成筆一枝也。問：「此物有何神通？」道士曰：「你不知我法家作用耳。這紙筆上，不知破了多少人家矣。」
stories.translation: A rascal was angry at a wealthy man and wanted to ruin his family but could not find a way. He heard that the Taoist priests of Mount Mao had the highest magical powers, so he went there and earnestly pleaded his case with them. The Taoist priest said, "I will send heavenly soldiers to secretly punish this man." He replied, "Even if his descendants remain wealthy, I am still not satisfied." The priest said, "Then I will let heavenly fire burn down his house and buildings." He replied, "His farmland still remains; I am still not satisfied." The Taoist priest said, "Is your hatred for him so deep!" "I have a most precious treasure. I will give it to you; take it and worship it day and night, and his family's fortune will naturally vanish immediately." The man was very pleased and asked to see it. It was sealed very tightly, but when opened, it turned out to be just a brush made of paper. He asked, "What divine power does this object have?" The Taoist priest said, "You don't know the power of our legalist methods." "This paper brush alone has ruined countless families."

stories.text: 有善相者，扯一人要相。其人曰：「我倒相著你了。」相者笑云：「你相我何如？」答曰：「我相你決是相不著的。」
stories.translation: lø A fortune teller grabbed a man and wanted to read his face. The man said, "I have already read your face." The fortune teller laughed and asked, "What did you see in me?" He replied, "I read that you are definitely someone who cannot be read."

stories.text: 一人善卜，又喜詼諧。有以孕之男女來問者，卜訖，拱手恭喜曰：「是個夾卵的。」其人喜甚，謂為男孕無疑矣。及產，卻是一女，因往咎之。卜者曰：「維男有卵，維女夾之。有夾卵之物者，非女子而何？」
stories.translation: A man was skilled in divination and also enjoyed witty remarks. When someone came to ask about the gender of a pregnancy, after making his divination, he bowed and congratulated them, saying, "It's a double-yolked one." The person was very pleased, thinking it was definitely going to be a boy. But when the child was born, it turned out to be a girl, so he went to blame him. The diviner said, "Only boys have yolks; girls are the ones with two." "There is something called a double yolk. If it's not a girl, then what else could it be?"

stories.text: 街市失火，延燒百餘戶。有星相二家欲移物以避，旁人止之曰：「汝兩家包管不著，空費搬移。」星相曰：「火已到矣，如何說這太平話？」曰：「你們從來是不著的，難道今日反會著起來！」
stories.translation: A fire broke out in the marketplace and spread to over a hundred households. Two families of fortune tellers wanted to move their belongings to avoid the fire, but a passerby stopped them and said, "The two of you are guaranteed not to be affected; it's just a waste of effort moving things." The fortune tellers said, "The fire has already reached us. How can you say such peaceful words?" The passerby replied, "You two have never been affected before; could it be that today you will suddenly catch fire!"

stories.text: 有寫真者，絕無生意。或勸他將自己夫妻畫一幅行樂貼出，人見方知。畫者乃依計而行。一日，丈人來望，因問：「此女是誰？」答云：「就是令愛。」又問：「他為甚與這面生人同坐？」
stories.translation: There was a portrait painter who had absolutely no business. Someone advised him to paint a portrait of himself and his wife as a couple, hang it outside for people to see, so that they would know about him. The painter followed the suggestion. One day, his father-in-law came to visit and asked, "Who is this woman?" He replied, "That's your daughter." The father-in-law asked again, "Why is she sitting with this unfamiliar man?"

stories.text: 一畫士寫真既就，謂主人曰：「請執途人而問之，試看肖否？」主人從之，初見一人問曰：「那一處最像？」其人曰：「方巾最像。」次見一人，又問曰：「那一處最像？」其人曰：「衣服最像。」及見第三人，畫士囑之曰：「方巾、衣服都有人說過，不勞再講，只問形體何如？」其人躊躇半晌，曰：「鬍鬚最像。」
stories.translation: A painter, having finished a portrait, told the owner, "Please bring in a passerby and ask him to see if it looks like you." The owner followed his suggestion. When they first saw one person, he was asked, "Which part resembles the most?" The passerby said, "The square headpiece looks most like." They then saw another person and asked again, "Which part resembles the most?" The passerby said, "The clothing looks most like." When they saw the third person, the painter instructed him, "The headpiece and clothing have already been mentioned by others; there is no need to repeat. Just ask how he looks in terms of physique." The passerby hesitated for a while and said, "The moustache looks most like."

stories.text: 有自負棋高，與人角，連負三局。次日，人問之曰：「昨日較棋幾局？」答曰：「三局。」又問：「勝負何如？」曰：「第一局我不曾贏，第二局他不曾輸，第三局我本等要和，他不肯罷了。」
stories.translation: There was a man who boasted of his high chess skills. After playing against others, he lost three consecutive games. The next day, someone asked him, "How many games did you play at chess yesterday?" He replied, "Three games." They asked again, "What was the result?" He said, "In the first game I did not win; in the second game he did not lose. In the third game, I wanted to draw, but he refused to stop."

stories.text: 一人以好棋破產，因而為小偷，被人縛住。有相識者，見而問之，答云：「彼請我下棋，嗔我棋好，遂相困耳。」客曰：「豈有此理？」其人答曰：「從來棋高一著，縛手縛腳。」
stories.translation: A man squandered his fortune on chess and thus became a thief, who was later caught and bound by others. Someone who knew him saw this and asked about it, to which he replied, "They invited me to play chess. They were annoyed that my chess was good, so they trapped me." The guest said, "How could such a thing happen?" The man replied, "Since ancient times, being just one move better at chess has led to bound hands and feet."

stories.text: 一人生子，慮其難養，請一星家算命。星士曰：「關煞倒也沒得，大來運限俱好，只是四柱中犯點賊星，不成正局。」那人曰：「不妨，只要養得大，就叫他學做銀匠。」星士曰：「為何？」答曰：「做了銀匠，那日不偷幾分養家活口。」
stories.translation: A man had a son and was worried about raising him, so he invited an astrologer to calculate the child's fortune. The astrologer said, "There is no harmful star to worry about; the major fortune and life span are all good. However, there is a thief star in his four pillars that disrupts the proper formation." The man said, "That's fine. As long as he grows up healthy, I'll have him learn to be a silversmith." The astrologer asked, "Why?" He replied, "Once he becomes a silversmith, he can steal a few coins every day to support the family."

stories.text: 銀匠開鋪三日，絕無一人進門。至暮，有以碎銀二錢來傾者，乃落其半，傾作對充與之。其人大怒，謂其利心太重。銀匠曰：「天下人的利心，再沒有輕過如我的。開了三日店，止落得一錢，難道自己吃了飯，三分一日，你就不要還了？」
stories.translation: On the third day of opening his shop, a silversmith saw not a single customer enter. By dusk, someone came in with two qian of broken silver to melt down. The silversmith took half of it and melted the rest into a pair of earrings for him. The man became very angry, saying that his greed was too great. The silversmith said, "No one in the world has a lighter sense of profit than I do." "I opened my shop for three days and only earned one qian. If you don't pay back the cost of your meal, which is three fen a day, how can I survive?"

stories.text: 一翁有三婿，長裁縫，次銀匠，惟第三者不學手藝，終日閑遊。翁責之曰：「做裁縫的，要落幾尺就是幾尺。做銀匠的，要落幾錢就是幾錢。獨汝遊手好閑，有何結局？」三婿曰：「不妨。待我打一把鐵竅，竅開人家庫門，要取論千論百，也是易事，稀罕他幾尺幾錢！」翁曰：「這等說，竟是賊了。」婿曰：「他們兩個，整日落人家東西，難道不是賊？」
stories.translation: An old man had three sons-in-law. The eldest was a tailor, the second a silversmith, and only the third one did not learn any trade, idling about all day long. The old man scolded him, saying, "A tailor can earn however many chi of cloth he cuts." "A silversmith earns however many qian of silver he melts down." "Only you are idle and lazy. What kind of future do you have?" The third son-in-law said, "That's fine." "Wait for me to forge an iron lock pick. Once I open the door of someone's warehouse, taking hundreds or even thousands is easy. Why should I care about a few chi of cloth or qian of silver!" The old man said, "If that's what you say, then you are truly a thief." The son-in-law replied, "Those two earn their living by taking things from others every day. Are they not also thieves?"

stories.text: 時年大旱，太守命法官祈雨。雨不至，太守怒，欲治之，法官稟云：「小道本事平常，不如其裁縫最好。」太守曰：「何以見得？」答曰：「他要落幾尺就是幾尺。」
stories.translation: At that time, there was a great drought. The governor ordered the judge to pray for rain. When the rain did not come, the governor became angry and wanted to punish him. The judge reported, "My humble skills are ordinary; it would be better to let a tailor do this." The governor asked, "Why is that?" He replied, "Because he can earn however many chi of fabric as he wants."

stories.text: 縫匠裁衣，反覆量，久不肯下剪。徒弟問其故，答曰：「有了他的，便沒有了我的。有了我的，又沒有了他的。」
stories.translation: A tailor was measuring fabric repeatedly while making a garment and refused to cut it for a long time. The apprentice asked why, and the tailor replied, "If I take more from his fabric, there will be less left for me." "If I take less for myself, then he will have too much left."

stories.text: 一裁縫上廁坑，以尺揮牆上，便完忘記而去。隨有一滿洲人登廁，偶見尺，將腰刀掛在上面。少頃，裁縫轉來取尺，見有滿人，畏而不前，觀望良久。滿人曰：「蠻子，你要甚麼？」答曰：「小的要尺。」滿人曰：「咱囚攮的，屙也沒有屙完，你就要吃（尺）！」
stories.translation: A tailor went to the latrine and used his measuring stick to scratch on the wall. After finishing, he forgot it and left. Soon after, a Manchu man went to the latrine, happened to see the measuring stick, and hung his waist knife on it. After a while, the tailor returned to retrieve his measuring stick but saw a Manchu man there and was afraid to approach. He hesitated for quite some time. The Manchu man said, "Mansi, what do you want?" He replied, "I need my measuring stick." The Manchu man said, "You rascal! I haven't even finished relieving myself yet, and you already want to take it (the stick)!"

stories.text: 一匠人裝門閂，誤裝門外，主人罵為「瞎賊」。匠答曰：「你便瞎賊！」主怒曰：「我如何倒瞎？」匠曰：「你若有眼，便不來請我這樣匠人。」
stories.translation: A carpenter installed a door latch but mistakenly put it on the outside. The homeowner scolded him as a "blind thief." The craftsman replied, "You are the blind thief!" The homeowner angrily asked, "How am I blind?" The craftsman said, "If you had eyes, you would not have come to hire a craftsman like me."

stories.text: 一人破家與一妓相處數年，臨別，妓女贈得陰毛數根，珍藏帽中，時為把玩。一日忽失去，遍尋不得。偶踱至街頭，遇一皮匠口含豬鬃縫鞋，其人罵而奪之曰：「我用盡銀錢，只落得這兩根毛，如何偷來倒插在你口裡面？」
stories.translation: A man, after squandering his fortune, had been in a relationship with a courtesan for several years. When they parted ways, the woman gave him a few strands of her pubic hair as a gift. He treasured them and kept them in his hat, often taking them out to play with. One day they suddenly went missing, and he searched everywhere without success. By chance, he strolled to the street and saw a cobbler holding pig bristles in his mouth while sewing shoes. The man scolded and snatched them, saying, "I spent all my silver just to get these two strands of hair. How could you steal them and stick them into your mouth?"

stories.text: 一待詔初學剃頭，每刀傷一處，則以一指掩之。已而傷多，不勝其掩，乃曰：「原來剃頭甚難，須得千手觀音來才好。」
stories.translation: A barber who was just learning to shave would cover each cut with a finger. Soon, the number of cuts became too many to cover, so he said, "Shaving is really difficult. One would need a thousand-armed Guanyin to do it properly."

stories.text: 篦頭者被賊偷竊。次日，至主顧家做生活，主人見其戚容，問其故。答曰：「一生辛苦所積，昨夜被盜。仔細想來，只當替賊篦了一世頭耳。」主人怒而逐之。他日另換一人，問曰：「某人原是府上主顧，如何不用？」主人為述前言，其人曰：「這樣不會講話的，只好出來弄卵。」
stories.translation: A hair comber was robbed by a thief. The next day, he went to his client's home for work. The client noticed his sorrowful expression and asked why. He replied, "All the hard-earned possessions I had accumulated were stolen last night." "When I think about it carefully, it's as if I've just spent a lifetime combing the hair of that thief instead." The client became angry and drove him away. Another day, when a new person was hired, he asked, "That man used to be your regular client. Why are you no longer using his services?" The owner explained the previous incident, and the new person said, "Someone who can't speak properly should just go out and mess with eggs."

stories.text: 一待詔替人剃頭，才舉手，便所傷甚多。乃停刀辭主人曰：「此頭尚嫩，下不得刀。且過幾時，姑俟其老再剃罷。」
stories.translation: A barber was shaving someone's head, and as soon as he raised his hand, he caused many cuts. He stopped cutting and said to the owner, "This head is still too soft for me to use a blade." "Just wait a while. Let it grow older before I shave it."

stories.text: 一待詔為人看耳，其人痛極，問曰：「左耳還取否？」曰：「方完，次及左矣。」其人曰：「我只道就是這樣取過去了。」
stories.translation: A barber was extracting an ear for someone, and the person in pain asked, "Shall I remove your left ear as well?" He replied, "The right one is just finished. It's now time for the left." The person said, "I thought it would be over with like this."

stories.text: 有善刻圖書者，偶于市中喚人修腳。腳已脫矣，修者正欲舉刀，見彼袖中取出一袱，內裹圖書刀數把。修者不知，以為剔腳刀也，遂絕然而去。追問其故。則曰：「同行中朋友，也來戲弄我。」
stories.translation: There was a man skilled in engraving seals who, by chance, called someone to trim his feet at the market. After his shoes were removed, just as the footbath worker was about to raise a knife, he saw that the man took out a cloth wrap from his sleeve containing several seal-carving knives. The footbath worker did not know what they were and thought they were just foot-trimming tools, so he left in alarm. He was later asked why he had left. He replied, "A friend from the same trade came to play a trick on me."

stories.text: 廚子往一富家治酒，竊肉一大塊，藏于帽內。適為主人窺見，有意作耍他拜揖，好使帽內肉跌下地來。乃曰：「廚司務，勞動你，我作揖奉謝。」廚子亦知主人已覺，恐跌出不好看相，急跪下曰：「相公若拜揖，小人竟下跪。」
stories.translation: A cook went to a wealthy household to prepare wine and stole a large piece of meat, hiding it inside his hat. Just then, the master happened to see this and decided to play a trick by making him bow deeply so that the meat in his hat would fall down. The master said, "Kitchen staff, you have worked hard for me. I will bow to thank you." The cook also realized the master had noticed and, fearing that the meat would fall out in an embarrassing way, quickly knelt down and said, "If Master bows, I must kneel."

stories.text: 一人睡倒，戲語人曰：「我好像一隻船，頭似船頭，腳似船尾，肚腹似船艙。」又指陽物曰：「這個豈不像撐船的？」人曰：「那裡有這等垂頭喪氣的家長。」答曰：「你不曉得，搖船的時節，從來是軟臘塔的，一到討船錢時，便硬掙得不像樣了。」
stories.translation: A man was lying down and jokingly said to others, "I look like a boat. My head is the bow of the boat, my feet are the stern, and my belly is the hold." He then pointed to his penis and said, "Doesn't this look like an oar for rowing a boat?" Someone replied, "Where is there such a dispirited and drooping family head?" He replied, "You don't know. When rowing a boat, it is always soft and drooping. But when it comes time to collect the fare, it becomes hard and stiff in no time."

stories.text: 梢公死，閻王判他變作陰戶。梢公不服，曰：「是物皆可做，為何獨變陰物？」閻王曰：「單取你開也會開，擺也會擺，又善搖，又善擺。」
stories.translation: A boatman died, and King Yama sentenced him to be reborn as a female genitalia. The boatman was不服 (unconvinced) and said, "Anything can be made into something else. Why must I specifically become a female genitalia?" King Yama said, "It's because you are good at opening and closing, swaying and moving. You were especially skilled in rowing and steering."

stories.text: 船家與妻同睡，夫摸著其妻陰戶，問曰：「此是何物？」妻曰：「是船艙。」妻亦握夫陽具，問是何物，答曰：「客貨。」妻曰：「既有客貨，何不裝入艙裡來？」夫遂與雲雨，而兩卵在外。妻以手摸曰：「索性一並裝入也罷。」夫曰：「這兩個是水手，要在後面看舵的。」
stories.translation: A boatman was sleeping with his wife. The husband touched her genitalia and asked, "What is this?" The wife said, "It's the hold of a boat." The wife also grasped her husband's penis and asked what it was. He replied, "It is cargo for passengers." The wife said, "If there is passenger cargo, why not load it into the hold?" The husband then had sexual intercourse with his wife, and both their genitalia remained outside. The wife reached out to touch it and said, "Might as well load them in together." The husband replied, "These two are sailors. They need to be at the back steering the rudder."

stories.text: 一家做酒，頗賣不去，以為家有耗神。請一先生燒椿退送，口念曰：「先除鷺鷥，後去青鸞。」主人曰：「此二鳥你退送他怎的？」先生曰：「你不知，都吃虧這兩隻禽鳥會下水，遣退了他，包你就賣得去！」
stories.translation: A family brewed alcohol, but it was not selling well. They thought there must be a spirit of waste in their home. They invited a master to perform a ritual, burning incense and chanting, "First remove the heron, then drive away the green phoenix." The host asked, "What are you driving these two birds away for?" The master said, "You don't know—these two birds are the reason. They can dive underwater and spoil your wine. If I drive them away, I guarantee you will be able to sell it!"

stories.text: 朝廷新開一例，凡物有兩名者充軍，三名者斬。茄子自覺雙名，躲在水中。水問曰：「你來為何？」茄曰：「避朝廷新例。因說我有兩名，一名茄子，一名落蘇。」水曰：「若是這等，我該斬了：一名水，二名湯，又有那天災人禍的放了幾粒米，把我來當酒賣。」
stories.translation: The imperial court recently established a new regulation: anyone who has two names will be conscripted into the army, and those with three names will be executed. Eggplant, realizing it had two names, hid in water. Water asked, "Why have you come?" Eggplant replied, "To avoid the new regulation of the imperial court." It explained that it had two names: one is qiezi and the other is luosu. Water said, "If that is the case, I should be executed too: I have one name as 'water,' a second as 'broth,' and then there was some disaster or misfortune when a few grains of rice were added, and they sold me as wine."

stories.text: 人問：「何為叫做酒娘？」答曰：「糯米加酒藥成漿便是。」又問：「既有酒娘，為甚沒有酒爺？」答曰：「放水下去，就是酒爺。」其人曰：「若如此說，你家的酒，是爺多娘少的了。」
stories.translation: Someone asked, "Why is it called 'wine mother'?" The answer was, "It is made by adding rice and wine yeast to form a broth." Another person asked, "If there is a 'wine mother,' why isn't there a 'wine father'?" The answer was, "Add water to it, and that becomes the wine father." That person said, "If that is how it works, then in your house there must be more 'wine fathers' and fewer 'wine mothers.'"

stories.text: 一店中釀方熟，適有帶巾者過，揖入使嘗之。嘗畢曰：「竟有些像我。」店主知其秀才也，謝去之。少焉，一女子過，又使嘗之，女子亦曰：「像我。」店主曰：「方才秀才官人說『像我』，是酸意了，你也說『像我』，此是為何？」女子曰：「無他，只是有些走作。」
stories.translation: In a shop, the newly brewed wine was just ready. At that moment, a man with a headscarf passed by; he was invited in and asked to taste it. After tasting it, the man said, "It actually tastes somewhat like me." The shop owner realized he was a scholar and politely sent him away. A short while later, a woman passed by; they asked her to taste it as well, and she also said, "It tastes like me." The shop owner asked, "Earlier the scholar said 'It tastes like me,' which meant it was sour. You also say 'It tastes like me.' What does that mean?" The woman replied, "Nothing else—it's just a bit off."

stories.text: 有賣酸酒者，客上店謂主人曰：「餚只腐菜足矣，酒須要好的。」少頃，店主問曰：「菜中可要著醋？」客曰：「醋滴菜心甚好。」又問曰：「腐內可要放些醋？」客曰：「醋烹豆腐也好。」再問曰：「酒內可要著醋否？」客訝曰：「酒中如何著得醋？」店主攢眉曰：「怎麼處？已著下去了。」
stories.translation: A wine seller, a customer came into the shop and told the owner, "The food is fine with just some pickled vegetables, but I must have good wine." After a while, the shop owner asked, "Do you want to add vinegar to the dish?" The customer said, "Dripping some vinegar into the center of the vegetable is very good." Then he was asked again, "Do you want to put some vinegar in the fermented food?" The customer replied, "Cooking tofu with vinegar is also good." Then he was asked once more, "Do you want to add some vinegar into the wine?" The customer was surprised and said, "How can vinegar be added to wine?" The shop owner frowned and said, "What should I do?" "It's already been added."

stories.text: 一酒家招牌上寫：「酒每斤八厘，醋每斤一分。」兩人入店沽酒，而酒甚酸。一人咂舌攢眉曰：「如何有此酸酒，莫不把醋錯拿了來？」友人忙捏其腿曰：「呆子，快莫做聲，你看牌面上寫著醋比酒更貴著哩！」
stories.translation: A wine shop had a sign that read, "Wine is eight li per jin, and vinegar is one fen per jin." Two men entered the store to buy wine, but the wine was very sour. One of them stuck out his tongue and frowned, saying, "How can there be such sour wine? Wasn't the vinegar mistakenly brought here?" His friend quickly pinched his leg and said, "Fool! Be quiet. Look at the sign—it says vinegar is even more expensive than wine!"

stories.text: 有以酸酒飲客者，個個攢眉，委吞不下。一人嘲之曰：「此酒我有易他良法，使他不酸。」主人曰：「請教。」客曰：「只將酒壇覆轉向天，底上用艾火連炙七次，明日拿起，自然不酸。」主曰：「豈不傾去漏乾了？」客曰：「這等酸酒，不傾去要他做甚！」
stories.translation: There was a person who served sour wine to guests, and every guest frowned and could not swallow it. One man mocked him and said, "I have an easy method to improve this wine so that it won't be sour." The host replied, "Please teach me." The guest said, "Just turn the wine jar upside down toward the sky and roast its bottom seven times with mugwort fire. When you take it out tomorrow, it will naturally no longer be sour." The host asked, "Won't the wine spill and run dry?" The guest replied, "Such sour wine—if it doesn't spill out, what good is it for!"
